Square basketry mat. Twill woven of blonde palm leaf material. Thick rim is make of bunched and wrapped palm leaves. [MOBB [OPS move] 13/12/2016]
Square basketry sieve. Slightly open twill woven basketry attached to a double frame of cane. [MOBB [OPS move] 25/11/2016]
Water container of gourd, with a stopper of leaves.
Fishing scoop consisting of a roughly triangular piece of open basketry tied to wooden loop and bound to a wooden handle. [MJD 20/11/2009]
Fishing rod made from a small sapling, stripped of bark except on the handle with metal hook and fine wild pineapple fibre cord.
Baby carrying sling. Made of cotton in the style of a small hammock, but circular instead of one strip. Finger woven on a frame. [ASh [OPS move] 15/2/2017]
Cylindrical basket with a band of cane around the rim. Decorated with a geometric tigers, fish, and dog design.  [BH [OPS Move] 16/11/2016]

Basketry tray. With a dyed stylised geometric scroll work design, supposedly in a caterpillar and puppy design. There is a line of cotton yarn stitched into the basketry where the base meets the sides. [BH [OPS Move] 8/12/2016]

Basketry Fire fan ?also used at mat & cassava cooking accessory. Rectangular in shape, with a bamboo stick running along the length, attached to the basketry by stitched plant fibre [BH [OPS move] 17/11/2016]
Tall cylindrical basket with a square base and round opening.
Square basketry tray, with a loose weave on the walls and a cord of stitched string attaching the sides to the base, which is decorated with geometric shapes. [BH [OPS move] 17/11/2016]
Basketry box. Rectangular box of blonde coloured palm leaf. The lid for this box is 1964.2.51 .2. [MOBB [OPS move] 16/11/2016]
Wooden stool comprising a rectangular seat and two rectangular planks jointed to the seat for legs. The seat has a central field carved with an interlacing ribbon design. [JC [OPS Move] 11/4/2017]

Angular fire fan woven in yellow plant fibre. The handle of the object is secured with black fibre string.
A used child's carrying basket, known as katali (palm leaf tump) and wama hale (arouman, ischnosiphon arouma) cane fibres on wooden frame), with a piece of tied black fibre and plant fibre straps.

Manale or sieve made of wama hale or arouman (Ischnosiphon arouma), used to sieve bricks of fried and squeezed bitter cassava. Square, with four cane supports on each side; woven with a central diamond design.
Kamina. Fish trap (kamina) for smaller fish. Made of straight, flat staves of bamboo (guadua angufolia) woven together with liana.

Kamina. Fish trap made of Aymara (bamboo (guadua angustifolia?), and liana). Conical trap of split bamboo staves woven together with vines. Circular lid tied to the trap with pale plant fibres. Two long twigs are joined to a wooden peg inserted through the narrow end. Part of a threaded plastic object tied inside. It was found abandoned under the house of Tompouce, whose father-in-law repaired it for the collectors.

Fish landing basket of wood and wama hale, arouman, Ischnosiphon. Pointed basket of open weave with an oval opening. Long handle joined to basket with cane wrapping. Handle broken during transportation to the museum.

Small paddle. The blades are both rounded; one tapers to a point, and the other is truncated with a flat edge and a triangular notch in both sides. The paddle is painted with black synthetic paint, except for the narrow central part where the wood retains its natural colour.
Round-bottomed basket with domed lid attached to long handle by a small loop. There is another small loop at the top of the lid. The basket is decorated with blue, green, yellow and red stripes.
A cotton baby sling. Woven into a cylindrical shape.

Nose flute made from two tubular sections of reed, closed at both ends [1964.2.105 .1 - .2]. [JMC 22/2/2019]
Notched flute of reed with a closed end. [JC [OPS Move] 31/1/2017]
Notched flute of reed with a closed end. [JC [OPS Move] 1/2/2017]

Notched flute of reed, open at the end. There are three finger-holes burnt into the reed in a vertical line. The upper half is bound with cotton fibre and a length of red textile. [JC [OPS Move] 1/2/2017]

Notched flute of reed, open at the end. There are three finger-holes burnt into the reed, four in a line and one to the side. The notched end of the flute is split, while the opposite end is bound with cotton string. [JC [OPS Move] 1/2/2017]
Flute. Made from a hollow length of reed and closed at both ends. There are two stops at each end, four in total. [AB [OPS Move] 2/2/2017]

Half of a nose flute, consisting of a tubular piece of reed, closed at one end. There are two stops near the closed end, which is coated in gum. The open end is narrow in order to slot into the reed that makes up the other half, [1964.2.105 .20 .1].

Half of a nose flute. Consisting of a tubular piece of reed, closed at one end. There are two stops near the closed end. The open end is narrow in order to slot into the reed that makes up the other half, [1964.2.105 .21 .1].
Section of duct flute. Made of reed. With one stop. Open at both ends, there is cotton tied around one end of the reed. For the major section of the flute see 1964.2.108 .1  [AB [OPS Move] 6/2/2017]

Reed for a clarinet. The reed is straight, one end is closed the other is sliced at an angle. There is a band of red coloured textile tied to the reed part-way along its length. For the clarinet please see 1964.2.99 .1  [AB [OPS Move] 17/2/2017]

Extension tube for single reed clarinet. Made from a hollow length of wood from the "congo pump" tree. It is cylindrical, one end is carved to taper slightly. For the clarinet see 1964.2.102 .1, for the reed see 1964.2.102 .3  [AB [OPS Move] 17/2/2017]
One of a pair of rattles. For the other in the pair please see 1964.2.72 .1 [AB [OPS Move] 6/2/2017]
Nose flute made from two tubular sections of reed, closed at both ends [.1-.2]. One piece [.1] has a binding of red textile at the open end. [AB [OPS Move] 1/2/2017]
Nose flute made from two tubular sections of reed, closed at both ends [1964.2.105 .19 .1 - .2]. [JMC 22/2/2019]
Notched flute of reed with a closed end. [JC [OPS Move] 31/1/2017]
Notched flute of reed with a closed end. There are six finger-holes burnt into the reed, four in a line and one to either side. [JC [OPS Move] 1/2/2017]

Notched flute of reed with a closed end. There are six finger-holes burnt into the reed, four in a line and two to one side near the closed end. The upper half of the flute is bound with very fine plant fibre. [JC [OPS Move] 1/2/2017]
Notched flute of reed, open at the end. There are three finger-holes burnt into the reed in a vertical line. The end is bound with cotton string to prevent further splitting. [JC [OPS Move] 1/2/2017]

Notched flute of reed, open at the end. There are three finger-holes burnt into the reed in a vertical line. The top of the flute is bound with fine plant fibre cord and a section below the finger holes is bound with cotton fibre. There is a small split which is coated in parts with gum and urucu dye, to prevent further splitting. [JC [OPS Move] 1/2/2017]
Notched flute of reed, open at the end. There are three finger-holes burnt into the reed in a vertical line. The end is bound with cotton string. [JC [OPS Move] 1/2/2017]

Notched flute made from a piece of plastic tubing, open at both ends. A perforated wax node is situated inside the flute. There are three finger-holes in a vertical line and a small area of string binding near the far end. [JC [OPS Move] 1/2/2017]

Half of a nose flute, consisting of a tubular piece of reed, closed at one end. There are two stops near the closed end, which is coated in gum. The open end has a binding of red textile. For the reed that makes up the other half see [1964.2.105 .20 .2].

Duct flute. Made from reed. One end of the reed is open, the other closed with a small perforation. There is a rectangular perforation in the body of the reed, within this is a nodule made of gum and black in colour. There is a strip of plant leaf wrapped around the flute and tied with plant fibre. [AB [OPS Move] 6/2/2017]

Single reed clarinet. Made from a hollow length of wood from the "congo pump" tree. It is cylindrical, one end is oblique, this end is split. Please note that there is no reed for this clarinet.  [AB [OPS Move] 17/2/2017]

Single reed clarinet. Made from a hollow length of wood from the "congo pump" tree. It is cylindrical, one end is notched. For the clarinet extension see 1964.2.102 .2, for the reed see 1964.2.102 .3  [AB [OPS Move] 17/2/2017]
Side-blown trumpet formed from a central reed attached to an armadillo claw and surrounded by two cones, one of palm leaf, one of split reed decorated with feathers. [JC [OPS Move] 2/2/2017]

Weyu. Beaded waist apron. Single trapeze length of fabric; narrow white waistband with twisted ties at both sides. Light and dark blue, woven bead work with red glass beaded border; two white horizontal beaded strips with a narrow red and white strip in the centre; white beaded geometrical forms. textile.title: Cotton thread. The string is quite thick and thought to be used for hammocks. The string is wound tightly around a small tube of cardboard.  [ASh [OPS move] 10/08/2016]
Wooden spindle with white cotton yarn. There is a hook carved at the end of the shaft. The whorl is made of gourd plant and has been incised with linear and zigzag patterns. [PR [OPS move] 26/4/2017]

String-work hammock, made from twisted cotton strands, threaded through intervals of transverse cotton bands. The suspension loops are made from dyed cotton, thickly bound with natural cotton.  [CW [OPS Move] 6/4/2017]
Kunana or stinging mat of woven palm fibre. A rectangular shaped piece of woven palm fibre with brown and white feathers adhered to the outer edge. Both sides of the mat are like this.

arms.title: Cotton thread. The string itself is very fine/thin and is used for leg bands and arrow making.  [ASh [OPS move] 10/08/2016]

Bow, made from wood. The bow tapers to a point at each tip. The bowstring, made from plant fibre, is tied to each tip of the bow. Tied along the length of the bow towards one end is the extending end of the bow string.  [SB [OPS move] 24/7/2017]

Wooden bow with pineapple fibre string. [El.B 21/2/2007]  For arrows see 1964.2.89.1-3 [HA 26/02/08
]

Bow, made from wood. The bow has a natural curve at each tip. Attached to each tip of the bow is the bowstring, made from twisted plant fibre, which is also bound to the bow at intervals with sections of plant fibre.  [SB [OPS move] 24/7/2017]
Bow, made of wood and strung with pineapple plant fibre cord. [ASh [OPS move] 24/7/2017]

bow; arrow - A set of Trio style bow and arrows. The bow (oulapa) is made of oulapa wood (ficus sp.?). The bow is probably strung with wulawaito (silk grass, bromelia sp.) and decorated with feathers from a species of toucan (ramphastos sp.) which are attached with cotton and silk grass.

club - Ornamental club made of wood and tusks of the white-lipped peccary (tayassu pecari). the handle is made of wama hale, arouman, Ischnosiphon arouma and bound with wulawaito (silk grass, bromelia sp.). It is decorated with feathers of kïnolo (scarlet macao, ara macao). ‘The club is mainly black with engraved designs and some brown painting. The lower part of the club has 2 tusks. Towards the pointy end there are bamboo strips tied with cotton. There is one multicoloured feather attached to the club. F. Veys, 13/6/2006’
Fishing arrow made of pÃ¯leu (wild cane, gynerium sagittatum) and bound with red and brown commercial cotton thread and wulawaito (silk grass, bromelia sp.) with double barbed steel tip.

sculpture.title: One miniature (perhaps child's) matapi, cassava squeezer (of wama hale, arouman, ischnosiphon arouma). Used to squeeze grated cassava in order to remove the juice.

ceramic.title: Brown ware pottery vessel with a short flat base, flaring sides and a flared rim. Plain, burnished exterior. [ASh [OPS move] 15/03/2016]
A large clay pot which was made by a woman for trade. These types of pots are rarely made for use now.

An oval clay pot which was made by a woman for trade. The pot is fired red. The central part of the body is painted white and black. The rim has been decorated with a cross-hatched motif in white and the central part on the inside has geometric decorations in white.
A small pot of red brown colour, with a straight rim, shoulders and a flat base.
